Application Materials.content:
Please upload supporting documents onto the [Graduate Admission System](https://gradapp.nus.edu.sg/portal/app_manage). The total size of uploaded documents should not exceed **10MB**. Documents should be saved as **PDF**. Documents not in English must be accompanied with certified copies of the English-translated version. Incomplete applications will not be considered. **You do not need to mail any documents during the application stage.** **Letters of recommendation, reference letters and referee details are not required to be submitted.**
- Your resume: updated resume detailing your educational background, internship and work experience (if any), achievements, etc.
- Copy of your official identification documents: Singapore Citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents should provide a copy of NRIC (front and back); international applicants should provide a copy of passport (identification page).
- Certified copies of your transcripts/mark sheets and degree certificate. Official transcripts and attested copy of degree scroll will be required after you are offered a place in the programme. Transcript Request Forms are available via this [link](https://msgfin.nus.edu.sg/wp-content/uploads/sites/125/sites/90/2022/09/Transcript-Request-Form.pdf).
- A Letter of Motivation: _Not more than 500 words_.

Interview Requirements.content: A strong performance in the interview (conducted for shortlisted candidates only).

All applicants will be notified of their outcomes no later than November.
Applications will only be reviewed if both the **application form is submitted** and the **application fee is paid** by the specified deadlines. Applications are valid for the immediate upcoming intake only.

Academic Requirements.content:
- A **good undergraduate degree in any discipline**.
- Applicants in the process of earning a degree or about to graduate are welcome to apply.
- **Work experience is not required** for admission into the programme. Applicants with some postgraduate work experience are also welcome to apply.

GRE GMAT Requirements.content:
**GMAT/GRE scores are optional**. Though it is not mandatory, a good GMAT or GRE score may enhance your application, particularly if your academic performance does not fully reflect your potential.
**Our institution code for this programme:**
- GMAT institution code: DRT-MK-69 (MSc in Real Estate)
- GRE institution code: 4642 – NUS Business School MSc Programmes
[More info on GMAT/GRE](https://mschcma.nus.edu.sg/faqs/)

English Proficiency Requirements.content: If English is not the native language or medium of prior undergraduate instruction: For **TOEFL**, the internet-based test score must be at least **5.0**. For **IELTS**, the overall band score must be at least **7.0**.

Program Overview.content:
The NUS MSc in Human Capital Management and Analytics is designed to equip the next generation of Human Capital Management leaders with future-ready human capital management skills and competencies. This programme is available both Full-Time and Part-Time.
This master’s degree is designed to equip recent graduates with future-ready human capital management skills and competencies. With significant developments in various human resources (HR) areas over the past 20 years, the HR function will demand talents with new and improved proficiencies, particularly in data analytics. The NUS Business School curriculum will combine functional human capital management capabilities with an analytical perspective, to help you transform data into actionable insights and develop suitable changes in the workplace.
The field of Human Capital Management is at a pivotal time in history. Organizations around the globe are navigating unprecedented challenges and opportunities: technological advancements, shifting employee expectations, the rise of data-driven decision-making, and increasing diversity. This program will help you harness analytics to drive strategic decisions, foster environments where people thrive, and ensure that organizations are equipped to meet the demands of a dynamic world.
**Emily M. David** is Academic Director, MSc in Human Capital Management and Analytics.
**Industries our graduates work in**
By Industry, graduates are hired across a wide range of industries such as:
- Banking & Financial Services
- Consulting & Market Research
- Consumer Goods
- Engineering & Manufacturing
- Distribution, Logistics & Supply Chain
- Public Sector
- Information Communications & Technology
By Job Function, graduates are involved in job functions such as:
- Human Resources Business Partner (HRBP)
- Regional Talent Acquisition Analytics Specialist
- Global HR Product Manager
- Human Capital Consultant
- Organizational Development Specialist
- People Analytics Specialist

Curriculum.content:
**12 Months. 44 Units.** The [MSc in Human Capital Management and Analytics](https://mschcma.nus.edu.sg/) programme is delivered intensively over **12 months** that includes an experiential learning component. Students are expected to complete **44 Units** to graduate. Please [click here](https://www.nus.edu.sg/registrar/calendar) for the NUS Academic Calendar.
| First Semester | Special Terms | Second Semester |
|---|---|---|
| Jan - Apr | May - Jul | Aug - Nov |
| 6 Courses (20 Units) | Experiential Learning (4 Units)* | 7 Courses (20 Units) |
*Alternatively, students can also do their experiential learning **after their second semester between JAN - APR**.
Courses are structured over 12 months. Full Course = 4 units (3 hours/week, 13 weeks duration); 2 units (3 hours/week 6-7 weeks duration).
- Artificial Intelligence for HR (4 Units)
- Communication for HR Professionals (2 Units)
- HR technology (2 Units)
- People Analytics (4 Units)
- Quantitative Methods for HR (4 Units)
- Talent Management (4 Units)
- Experiential Learning (4 Units): through an individual industry internship, faculty research project or a HR consultancy project. These internships and applied projects are primarily self-sourced.
- Compensation and Performance Management (4 Units)
- Ethics in Human Resource (2 Units)
- HR as Strategic Partner for Growth and Transformation (2 Units)
- Labour and Employment Law (2 Units)
- Leading and Managing Difficult Employees (2 Units)
- Negotiation and Dispute Resolution (4 Units)
- Talent Assessment & Selection (4 Units)
*The curriculum is subject to changes. The University reserves the right to revise the curriculum.
To graduate from the NUS MSc in Human Capital Management and Analytics programme, students must complete the programme requirements and achieve a Grade Point Average (GPA) of at least **3.2 (out of 5.0)**.

Cost of Attendance.content:
The estimated monthly living expenses for an international student in Singapore are outlined below:
| Expense Type | Cost |
| --- | --- |
| Accommodation | [On-campus housing](https://www.nus.edu.sg/osa/student-services/hostel-admission/graduate/hostel-options) (subject to availability): S$900 – S$1,800; Renting a room in a public housing apartment: S$700 – S$1,000; Renting a room in a private apartment: S$1,000 – S$2,000; Renting a 3-bedroom private apartment: S$4,000 onward |
| Meals | S$300 – S$800 |
| Transport (within Singapore) | S$80 – S$200 (buses and trains) |
| Healthcare | S$52 – S$112 per consultation with a General Practitioner |
| Personal Expenses | S$200 – S$350 |
| Mobile phone & broadband subscription | S$98 – S$280 |
Actual amounts will vary, depending on the individual’s lifestyle, but you should budget a minimum of **S$19,500 per year** for living expenses in Singapore. Sources: [EDB Singapore and NUS Hostel](https://www.edb.gov.sg/en/setting-up-in-singapore/cost-of-living-calculator.html) & [Meal Plan Rates](http://nus.edu.sg/osa/housing/graduate/hostel-and-meal-plan-rates.html)

Financial Aid.content:
Limited Full Scholarship & study awards are available for selected outstanding applicants. Study awards will cover a portion of the programme fees. There is no need to apply separately for the study awards and scholarships, but candidates must submit an application by the [first cut-off date](https://mim.nus.edu.sg/fees-finances/awards/). Study award and scholarship recipients are chosen based on merit in the following categories:
- **Excellence**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who have done exceptionally well in their academics, as well as during the application process (e.g. interviews).
- **Diversity**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who come from diverse personal and professional backgrounds and experience, and can contribute to the overall experience of their cohort.
- **Resilience**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who have demonstrated determination and resilience to achieve excellence in spite of adversity and hardship.
- **Achievers**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who have achievements in activities outside of the classroom, e.g. promoting or contributing to the UN SDGs; community service in social, environment, or other sectors; entrepreneurship, etc.
- **Local Candidates**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who are Singaporeans or Singapore PRs.
- **ASEAN Candidates**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who are nationals of an ASEAN country.
- **NUS Alumni**: This study award is given to outstanding candidate(s) who are NUS Alumni.

Multiple Applications.content: **I have applied for two different programmes through the online admission system. Ther are different sets of “Checklists”. Is this correct?** Yes, different programmes have different set-up for their “checklists” as different faculties/programmes have different requirements.
